evals.prompt: Add a marking rubric to my Year 10 Textiles workbooklet: 4 criteria (Research, Design development, Construction, Evaluation) across grades A to E, with a sentence or two per cell. It's a saddle-stapled booklet.
evals.expected_output: Chooses landscape (5 level columns plus a criterion column), keeps the preferred 27 cm by redistributing to 7 + 4x5 cm (or justifies 26 cm = 6 + 4x5 if the criterion text is short), 1.2 cm booklet landscape margins, a landscape section that returns to portrait with continuous page numbering, a repeating header row with White Table Heading on an Accent 5/6 fill, cantSplit rows, table alt text, and a check that the page count is still a multiple of 4.

evals.prompt: Make a glossary table of 30 elements and principles of design terms with definitions and a column for students to draw or write an example.
evals.expected_output: Stays portrait at 19 cm (long, not wide), columns in whole cm adding to 19 (e.g. 4 + 9 + 6), example column at least 4 cm, response rows set to at-least heights, a repeating header row, no row splitting, logical page breaks between groups, no landscape section.

evals.prompt: I want students to compare three posters side by side: the image, the designer, and how each one uses contrast, balance and emphasis, then write their own judgement underneath.
evals.expected_output: Considers landscape via the numeric test (3 images at 5 cm or more), selects 27 cm with 9 + 9 + 9 (or justifies a vertical category column with a whole-cm alternative), edge-to-edge image cells with zero padding and a common crop ratio, alt text on each image, a response row with a minimum height, and checks the table fits the roughly 16 cm landscape body height.

evals.prompt: Put a two-column table in the worksheet listing the 7 elements of design with a one-line description each. Flat printout, not a booklet.
evals.expected_output: Portrait at 19 cm (or 18 cm with a stated reason), a label column of about 3-4 cm and a description column taking the rest in whole cm, centred, no vertical category column (single group), header row in Heading 4 on a Pale fill, fits on one page, no landscape.

evals.prompt: Make a before-and-after table: two equal columns, one headed 'Before redesign' and one 'After redesign', with a photo and three bullet points of changes in each.
evals.expected_output: Identifies an image comparison of 2 items, stays portrait at the preferred 19 cm with 9.5 + 9.5 cm (not dropping to 18 cm just to avoid a half centimetre), header row in Heading 4 on a Pale fill, images inline and sized to the column, common crop ratio, alt text on both images, centred table.

evals.prompt: Create a table comparing 8 types of fabric across fibre, weave, weight, drape, care, cost and typical use.
evals.expected_output: Recognises 7 attributes would exceed 5 content columns in portrait, considers transposing (fabrics across the top would be 8 columns, so instead keeps fabrics down the page) and chooses landscape at 27 or 26 cm with a fabric label column plus attribute columns above their minimum widths in whole cm, or justifies a split into two portrait tables; header row repeats; rows do not split.
